historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-31.9%/5yr) is unusable and wildly divergent from revenue CAGR (+10.3%/5yr): shareholders' equity collapsed from $13.2m (FY2021) to $1.9m (FY2026) on a $7.7m FY2023 impairment/loss and continued FY2025-26 losses, not on distributions or a shrinking business -- the top line has grown every year. EPS and FCF CAGRs are not meaningful either: EPS has been negative in 4 of the last 6 years (no stable base to compound from) and owner FCF (reported FCF less IFRS-16 lease principal) was negative in FY2022, FY2023, FY2025 and FY2026 -- only FY2021 and FY2024 were positive. Selected growth_rate uses the 3yr REVENUE CAGR (8.2%) as the least-distorted top-line signal; it is explicitly NOT read as an owner-FCF or earnings growth rate, and the base-case forward path decelerates from it rather than assuming it continues, given the FY2026 margin collapse.

scenario_narratives.base: Strategic reset delivers a slow, partial margin recovery on continued mid-single-digit revenue growth; the business muddles through its liquidity strain without a further rescue raise but never approaches its FY2021 margin peak.
scenario_narratives.bull: Exo-migration capture, a fast and effective leadership reset, and a favourable Datagate exit combine to push margins back toward the FY2021 peak — several independent good outcomes, hence the lowest weight.
scenario_narratives.bear: The auditor's going-concern flag proves prescient: margins stay negative through a leadership vacuum and competitive Exo-migration leakage, and the balance sheet strain forces a further deeply dilutive raise or a covenant event.

valuation_philosophy.summary: ENS.NZ is valued as a going, revenue-growing operating business under real and disclosed going-concern stress -- an owner-FCF DCF, not a receivership/asset-waterfall model, because the company continues to trade, generated positive group operating cash flow in FY2026, and has a credible (if uncertain) forward cash-generating thesis in the forced MYOB Exo-to-Acumatica migration of its ~800-client installed base. The going-concern risk that a pure growth DCF would miss is priced three ways rather than folded silently into growth assumptions: a 20% WACC carrying an explicit +3pp going-concern/covenant premium on top of the NZ small-cap/illiquidity base, a 35% bear-case probability weight (the top of the method's going-concern band), and a bear scenario whose driver path is a genuine equity-impairment branch (sustained negative margins, a further dilutive raise or covenant breach) rather than merely 'growth disappoints'. Net debt is stated on a bank-borrowings-only basis (-$0.503m, i.e. net cash) because the lease liability is already fully charged through the flows under the consistent lease treatment used here -- so the going-concern strain in this model is a profitability/working-capital problem, not a heavy net-debt overhang, and the valuation should be read that way.
key_risks_to_valuation: Going-concern material uncertainty (FY2025 audit) and a worsening current ratio (0.69 -> 0.60) mean the base case's 'muddles through without a further raise' assumption could be wrong within the next 12 months -- a further rescue raise would dilute per-share value below every scenario computed here

No formal FY2027 guidance exists (management has committed only to a qualitative 'return to sustainable profitability'), so every driver path beyond the going-concern facts themselves is this model's judgment, not a disclosed target

CEO transition and an unscoped strategic review could produce further impairments, a divestiture (Datagate flagged for 'exit considerations'), or restructuring costs not modelled explicitly in any scenario

NCI (Recipe Marketing, iSell minority stakes) is consolidated into group OCF/capex rather than explicitly stripped from owner FCF -- a simplification given data granularity that could overstate attributable owner FCF by a small amount
Single-vendor (MYOB) dependency means the entire valuation is exposed to a platform-partner decision outside the company's control

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 0.375-0.725
data_sources.financials: research/ENS.NZ/Reports/ENS.NZ_Metrics.csv (financial-parser rebuild, FY2018-FY2026, all periods in NZD millions, EPS in dollars); FY2026 annual results announcement research/ENS.NZ/Extracted/ENS.NZ_Annual_FY2026.txt for balance sheet, cash flow and lease/borrowings detail
data_sources.qualitative: research/ENS.NZ/Reports/ENS.NZ_Analysis.json (qualitative-analyst, 2026-09-26) -- going-concern qualification, NZSA review findings, CEO departure, strategic reset, Exo migration thesis, Datagate exit considerations

inputs.sbc_source: Metrics.csv StockBasedComp column is 0.0 in every FY since FY2018 (financial-parser verified); no share-based-payment expense disclosed in the FY2026 annual. SBC-zero market treatment applies (owner-fcf-adaptations.md).
inputs.wacc_rationale: 20.0% = 11.5% NZ small-cap base (per AGL.NZ/2CC.NZ template) + 3.0% going-concern/covenant-breach premium (FY2025 audited accounts carried a going-concern material uncertainty per NZ Shareholders' Association review; current ratio worsened from 0.69 (FY2025) to 0.60 (FY2026), net assets fell $3.06m->$1.56m) + 2.5% illiquidity (micro-cap; market cap is a small multiple of the ~22.06m shares outstanding at current_price) + 1.5% single-vendor concentration (Kilimanjaro's earnings depend almost entirely on MYOB's Acumatica/Exo partner economics) + 1.5% leadership-transition/execution (20-year founder-CEO departed 4 Sep 2026 days after the Board called FY2026 'unacceptable'; interim CEO, ongoing strategic review, elevated recent board turnover). Risk is charged once, in this single WACC plus the bear-case weight -- not stacked again as a per-scenario WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B: IFRS-16 lease principal AND interest are deducted from owner FCF each year (lease_cost_pct_path), because interest paid (incl. lease interest) is already inside operating cash flow per the FY2026 cash-flow statement and lease principal repayment ($518k FY2026, $409k FY2025) sits in financing and is not otherwise captured. Lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net_debt/total_debt to avoid double-counting -- net_debt uses BANK BORROWINGS ONLY ($0.950m) less cash ($1.453m) = -$0.503m (net cash on a bank-debt basis). Total group debt including both lease tranches is $2.964m, but $2.014m of that is the lease liability already charged through the flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows and last_fcf are built on GROUP OCF/capex (not split by NCI), but net_income/EPS history and the equity bridge are attributable-to-owners only (FY2026 attributable NPAT -$2.032m vs group NPAT -$2.192m, NCI share -$160k in Recipe Marketing (48% NCI) and iSell (27.5% NCI)). No separate NCI deduction is applied to owner FCF because the NCI subsidiaries are small relative to Kilimanjaro and their cash flows are consolidated in OCF; this is a simplification given data granularity, noted as a modest source of imprecision (NCI is charged nowhere near twice, but also not explicitly stripped from the FCF stream) -- flagged in valuation_philosophy.key_risks_to_valuation.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: owner-FCF DCF (scenario-weighted, heavy bear weight), NOT the routing table's 'distressed/receivership/cash shell -> asset or creditor waterfall' row. ENS.NZ is trading normally on the NZX (not suspended, not in receivership, not delisted), still generated positive group operating cash flow in FY2026 ($0.512m) and has a real forward cash-generating thesis (Kilimanjaro's ~800-client MYOB Exo-to-Acumatica forced-migration pipeline, Exo compliance support ending Oct-2026). This matches the SML.NZ precedent (going-concern qualified but operating, scenario-weighted owner-FCF DCF with a bear case that can go negative) rather than the RUA.NZ precedent (audit DISCLAIMER + structurally negative owner FCF with no realistic path to positive flows, where no DCF is possible at all). Going-concern risk is priced via (a) a 20% WACC carrying an explicit going-concern premium, (b) a 35% bear weight (top of the 25-35%+ band the method specifies for going-concern situations), and (c) a bear case whose terminal FCF is allowed to hit the zero floor if the numbers say so -- not by abandoning the DCF framework. First valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF or memory entry exists.

bear.narrative: The going-concern risk the FY2025 auditor flagged materializes: the strategic reset fails to restore margins quickly enough against 'ongoing margin pressure in consulting services' and ~81%-of-revenue employee costs, the Exo migration wave leaks to competing Acumatica partners during the CEO/board transition vacuum, and further net losses push net assets toward zero or negative, forcing either a deeply dilutive rescue rights issue (as the Dec-2025/Jan-2026 raise already previewed) or a covenant breach on the BNZ facilities. Revenue contracts for three years before stabilising; EBITDA margin stays negative through year 3 and only turns marginally positive late in the horizon. Cash tax stays at zero throughout most of the horizon (accumulating, not using, tax losses) reflecting persistent unprofitability. This is the branch capturing genuine equity-impairment/insolvency risk, not merely a slower-growth base case -- consistent with the 35% weight, the top of the method's going-concern band.

base.narrative: The Board's post-FY2026 'strategic reset' (cost discipline, the Exo-to-Acumatica migration pipeline, Recipe Marketing/iSell cross-sell) delivers a gradual, unspectacular margin recovery -- EBITDA margin climbs from FY2026's -1.0% to a mid-cycle ~5% by year 8-9, still well below the FY2021 peak of 12.3%, reflecting genuinely thin consulting economics and no assumption that a new CEO instantly fixes the cost base. Revenue growth decelerates from the recent 3yr CAGR (8.2%, running above management's own description of 'subdued market conditions') toward a 2.5% terminal rate. Cash tax stays at/near zero for two years (NZ tax-loss carryforwards built up over FY2022-26's cumulative losses) before ramping to the 28% statutory rate by year 7. The going-concern liquidity strain is not modelled as a scenario-specific event here (it is priced in the WACC and the bear weight instead) -- this path assumes the company muddles through without a further rescue raise, which is itself an optimistic-of-median assumption given the current ratio and covenant position.

bull.narrative: Kilimanjaro converts the ~800-client Exo book into Acumatica revenue faster and more profitably than base as competing partners fail to keep pace with the Oct-2026 compliance-support deadline ('best partner standing' thesis working); a capable permanent CEO is appointed quickly and executes the strategic reset with real cost discipline; Recipe Marketing's HubSpot Diamond Partner momentum and iSell's international SaaS distribution both scale meaningfully; and the Datagate stake (32.35%) is monetised on favourable terms, providing both a cash injection (captured in the equity bridge, not the flows) and validation of the portfolio strategy. EBITDA margin recovers most of the way back to the FY2021 peak (12.3%) by year 5, settling at a 10% mature margin. This case requires several genuinely independent things to go right at once (leadership, execution, vendor dynamics, and a portfolio exit), which is why it carries the lowest of the three weights.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 10x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weighted at 35% (top of the method's 25-35%+ going-concern band) because this is not a hypothetical risk -- the FY2025 audited accounts carry an actual auditor going-concern material uncertainty, the current ratio has deteriorated for two straight periods (0.69 -> 0.60), net assets nearly halved in FY2026 alone, and the 20-year founder-CEO departed days after the Board itself called the result 'unacceptable'. Base held at 45% (below the house default 50%) because 'muddling through without a further raise' is itself an above-median outcome given two dilutive rights issues in the last three years. Bull trimmed to 20% because it requires several independent things to go right simultaneously (fast CEO appointment, Exo-conversion execution, Datagate monetisation, margin recovery) during an active strategic review whose scope and cost are explicitly not yet known.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
